text:
alex: Hey team — customer (acme_inc) sees intermittent SSE disconnects only when traffic flows through our SNI proxy/ingress. Direct-to-ingress-host works fine. Can someone help craft a minimal curl repro + a short checklist for the debug bundle? Request info: x-request-id=r-0a1b2c, trace=trace-82fa, seen around 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z.

sam: Thanks — can you paste the full x-request-id value and the client IP (if available)? Also is this HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 from the client side?

alex: full header was `x-request-id: r-0a1b2c-9f4d`. Client says HTTP/2. Client was behind a corporate proxy which uses SNI multiplexing to upstream.

maria: Quick repro I'd try to rule out SNI/Host mismatch: use `--resolve` to force the hostname -> proxy IP so curl sets SNI and Host correctly. Minimal streaming command we use internally: 

```
curl -v -N --http2 \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "x-request-id: r-0a1b2c-9f4d" \ 
  --resolve "api.redwood.example:443:1.2.3.4" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-2"
```

Notes: `-N`/`--no-buffer` keeps stdout streaming, `-v` shows the TLS handshake/SNI, `--http2` forces HTTP/2 to match client. Replace 1.2.3.4 with the proxy IP.

jin: Also collect these items when you run the curl so we can correlate: 
- `tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap host 1.2.3.4 and port 443` (capture TLS handshake timing)
- nginx/access + upstream/error logs for the same minute (include request_id)
- client-side verbose curl output (`curl -v`) and curl raw body dump (`curl --raw -o /tmp/body.dump`)

maria: If the proxy is SNI multiplexing multiple customers on same IP, add an explicit `Host:` header to the curl too (some proxies use ALPN/SNI mismatch): `-H "Host: api.redwood.example"`. Also try with and without `--http2` to see fallback differences.

sam: For auth, please redact the bearer token but include the token length (e.g. 64 chars) and whether it was rotated recently. If the token was short-lived, include the token issue time.

support-bot: I can assemble a minimal debug bundle template — please upload the following: `curl -v` stdout, tcpdump (pcap), nginx access+error lines (with timestamps), and a short reproduction note (time, account id, client IP). Use our internal upload link: https://uploads.redwood.internal/debug (mask tokens).

alex: Copying customer with steps. I'll run the two curl variants (with/without http2) and grab pcap + logs, then upload. Will post the upload link here.

jin: One more quick tip — if you see `TLS handshake: no shared cipher` or abrupt FIN after handshake in the pcap, that's usually proxy-level connection pooling or SNI routing killing the stream. If we have that, we should check upstream keepalive and `proxy_ssl_server_name` settings.

maria: If you get a reproducible case, try adding `--http1.1 -H "Connection: keep-alive"` to force HTTP/1.1 keepalive behavior; helps tell whether it's an HTTP/2 stream reset vs connection closed.

sam: Perfect — if you can include the exact curl stdout (`-v`) we can search for `:status` frames and `RST_STREAM` in the trace.

alex: Uploaded bundle at https://uploads.redwood.internal/debug/r-0a1b2c-20260315.tar.gz (redacted token inside). Ping me if you want me to repro from our test runner too. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Bundle received and attached to ticket #SUP-9921. Automatch found the nginx lines with `r-0a1b2c-9f4d`. Assigning to infra triage.

jin: I'll pick this up — thanks for the bundle. If I need anything extra I'll ask for a short tcpdump clipped to 10s around the handshake.

alex: thanks all, keeping customer updated.
